messages:
anne: quick thread — were seeing p99 spikes when inference clients hit obs-ingest and we batch small traces. batching helps cost but adds ~200-400ms for tiny inference traces. thinking about a 'gateway fastpass' path to keep latency-sensitive telemetry unbatched. pros/cons?

sam: do you mean per-request opt-out of batching? curious where the signal lives (header vs envelope attr).

anne: yes. two options im considering: 1) header at ingress (gateway reads and routes to fastpath service) 2) envelope attr (late enrichment decides) — header lets us avoid enqueueing entirely.

miguel: header is simplest for perf. but fastpath will blow up costs if abused. need rate limiting / quotas.

ria: also need to preserve billing attribution if we bypass coalescer. fastpath must attach the same billing keys and sampling tags so cost reports remain accurate.

sam: +1 on header, but we should standardize header name and schema. proposal: // X-Redwood-Obs-Priority: high | normal | background // and X-Redwood-Obs-Reason: inference | rollout | debug

anne: sketch for gateway routing rule:
```
if req.headers['x-redwood-obs-priority'] == 'high' and client-tier != 'debug':
    route_to = 'obs-fastpass'
else:
    route_to = 'obs-coalescer'
```

jen: rollout plan: feature-flagged canary for a subset of inference backends, monitor p50/p95/p99, cost-per-event. also add token-bucket limiter on fastpass (burst 100/s per org, sustained 10/s).

miguel: token-bucket sounds right. we should also emit metrics for how many events took fastpass vs batched so billing reconciliation can account. name them like: obs.fastpass.count and obs.coalesce.count with org tag.

ria: we must ensure downstream enrichment services can still enrich the fastpass events synchronously or have a fallback async join. otherwise queries will miss attributes and cost attribution will be wrong.

sam: alternative: fastpass doesn't skip enrichment, it just bypasses batching queue but still calls enrichment service synchronously (keeps semantic parity). that increases latency a little but keeps data correctness.

anne: good point. tradeoffs: fully bypassing enrich saves latency but risks incomplete attrib. sync enrichment keeps correctness but may reintroduce latency. need SLO targets.

jen: propose SLOs: fastpass p95 < 120ms for gateway->store and p99 < 300ms. if enrichment push makes this impossible, we degrade to 'fastmeta' mode where we attach minimal billing keys at gateway and async-enrich later (with marker for later join).

miguel: if we do later-join, add a determinism key (trace_id) and a join TTL. queries that need billing should be marked in UI/docs as eventual-consistent.

sam: small nit: use header boolean? but enum is better for future (background, low, normal, high). also document client SDK helpers so apps can set priority without fiddling headers.

anne: operational concerns: 1) observability of fastpath (traces, errors), 2) throttling/blacklist UI for orgs abusing it, 3) cost chargeback mapping.

ria: on cost mapping: ensure every fastpass increments the same billing counters as a coalesced event. if we use different ingestion pipeline, we must copy billing tags verbatim. we should add an ingest-test suite that asserts parity.

jen: rollout checklist (short):
- config + header contract doc (API)
- gateway routing + token-bucket limiter
- fastpass service that calls enrichment sync or fastmeta fallback
- metrics: obs.fastpass.count, obs.fastpass.latency p50/p95/p99, obs.fastpass.apply_rate
- feature flag + canary customers
- cost reconciler test (local sim)

deploy-bot: anne deployed gateway-fastpass-experiment -> canary cluster (obs-canary-1). watch obs.fastpass.latency.

anne: action items: sam to draft header + SDK helper, miguel to design token-bucket and throttle UI, ria to spec billing parity tests, jen to own rollout checklist + dashboards. i'll wire the gateway rule and enable canary for two inference customers tomorrow.

sam: happy to draft header + quick spec. will add example client snippet for node/python.

miguel: i'll mock cost delta in staging (run 10k events fastpass vs batched) and share numbers.

ria: i'll write the billing parity tests and a query tutorial for ops to interpret eventual joins.

anne: thanks all. keeping thread open for followups — if anyone wants to join canary review tomorrow ping me. :thumbsup:
